title: Detecting a quasi-isomorphism of perfect complexes on a neighbourhood
statement: For a chain map between strictly perfect complexes on an affine open, if its induced map on the stalk complex at a point is a quasi-isomorphism, then it is a quasi-isomorphism after restricting to some affine open containing the point and contained in the original open [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-perfect-complex] [def-pc-module-stalk-functor].

proof.text: Use the affine correspondence to replace the two complexes by bounded complexes of finite projective modules. The cone is again bounded finite projective, and the stalk hypothesis makes its localized derived object zero. The identity and zero endomorphisms of the cone agree after the filtered colimit of principal localizations, by injectivity of the perfect Hom comparison, so they agree on one principal localization. The cone is then zero there; the cone triangle proves the restricted map is a quasi-isomorphism, and the affine correspondence transports it back.
